newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1997 C/A gap seen at 6 pct GDP or lower.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1997 C/A gap seen at 6 pct GDP or lower.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Wednesday forecast that the 1997 current account deficit would be around or below six percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
He told reporters that so far the accumulated deficit recorded this year was lower than that projected by the Bank of Thailand.
"Last year our current account was around eight percent of GDP. But for this year, it is quite clear that the gap will narrow to around six percent or lower," he said.
Analysts said Thailand's high current account deficit was a major concern as it was financed mostly by foreign fund inflows.
The government in March announced massive spending cuts in an attempt to reduce the deficit.
Amnuay also said interest rates were likely to ease later this year, due to more stable interbank rate.
"The central bank reported that with this level of liquidity, interest rates have tendencies to ease," he said, adding "But I cannot tell when. It all depends on the market mechanism."
